title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.
summary: This work proves that the Markov length, a useful measure for characterizing quantum phases, is not robust against weak local noise channels. The instability manifests as an algebraic decay of the conditional mutual information, even when the channels are nearly identity operations. This challenges current theoretical frameworks that rely on the stability of such quantities for defining phase equivalence.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability of the Markov length, a quantity used to characterize mixed-state phases of matter, under the influence of weak local quantum channels.
main_result: The Markov length is generally unstable under weak local channels, failing even for pure product states due to algebraic decay of the conditional mutual information (CMI).
method: The authors use asymptotic analysis, Fourier methods, and spectral analysis of correlation matrices derived from Gaussian states to calculate the decay rates of the CMI.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on one-dimensional fermionic chains, generalized to bosonic and qubit chains, focusing on translation-invariant states with local rank deficiency.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), von Neumann entropy, and the Markov length ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Channel strength ($\epsilon$), system size ($N$), and the nature of the local channels (e.g., Gaussian channels).
main_assumptions: The instability is shown to hold for any translation-invariant state possessing at least one rank-deficient reduced density operator.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry defining the Markov length, while Figure 2 shows the gate structure of the depth-two channel acting on a fermionic chain.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the definition of the Markov length via CMI, demonstrates the instability using a fermionic chain model, analyzes the algebraic decay rooted in spectral properties, and discusses the implications for phase equivalence.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical challenge to definitions of phase equivalence in quantum many-body systems by showing that simple local perturbations can destroy key long-range order parameters.
